title: Day and night: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: At night, we see the Moon and stars.
The Sun shines only in the daytime.
The side of Earth turned away from the Sun has nighttime.
A place that has day will always have day.
Earth takes about 12 hours to turn one full time.
What do we call the spinning of Earth?
How much of Earth faces the Sun at a time?
items.why: “But only one side of Earth faces the Sun at a time.”

items.q: What is it on the side of Earth that gets light?
items.why: “That side gets light. That is daytime.”

items.q: How long does Earth take to turn one full time?
items.why: “Earth takes about 24 hours to turn one full time.”

items.q: How many times does Earth turn every day?

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: Earth is always spinning. The side of Earth that faces the Sun has day, and the side turned away from the Sun has night. Earth turns once every day, so day and night happen again and again.
Rotation is the spinning of Earth. Earth spins around and around.

items.q: Why is it dark on one side of Earth?
items.model: That side is turned away from the Sun, so it does not get sunlight.

items.q: Why does a place that has day later have night?
What do you like to do in the daytime? What do you do at night?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the ideas in the order of the text.
items: One side of Earth faces the Sun and has day
The other side is turned away and has night
A place that has day will later have night
